entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: `@ end()` modifier requires query range context (use LowerAt)
entries.rationale: the query endpoints always lower via LowerAtRange with the request window, so range context is always present; plain Lower is reached only from the matcher-metadata path, which carries no @ modifiers. Re-verified after expHistogramRangeFnWindowed replaced expHistogramRateWindowed: it resolves its anchor from the same lowerRoot dispatch under the same entry points, so it adds no path that reaches this switch with an empty range context. lowerExpHistogramBareMatrix (cerberus issue #2548) resolves its anchor from vs via this same anchorFromSelector under the identical LowerAt/LowerAtRange entry points its float-selector sibling lowerMatrixSelector already uses, so it adds no such path either. lowerAbsenceOverWindow is a new caller as of this change: it is the body lowerAbsentOverTime already had, extracted so that instant absent(<selector>) shares it rather than lowering to an unwindowed row count. Both absent() and absent_over_time() are function calls dispatched from lowerRoot under those same entry points, so the extraction moves no code across an entry-point boundary and adds no path that reaches this switch with an empty range context. It does mean absent(v @ start()) now reports this rejection where it previously ignored the modifier outright, which is the same answer its absent_over_time sibling has always given.

entries.head: promql
entries.rationale: the parser yields only START / END / 0 in StartOrEnd. The claim is a property of the parser rather than of any caller, so neither the expanded histogram range-function caller set, lowerExpHistogramBareMatrix (cerberus issue #2548), nor lowerAbsenceOverWindow — the extracted lowerAbsentOverTime body that instant absent(<selector>) now shares — can bear on it: the claim does not depend on which caller supplies vs.

guard: default of switch vs.StartOrEnd over [case parser.START; case parser.END; case 0; default]
